compiled_state.description:
## Testing Mode
RED then GREEN

## Story DD Coverage
This task is responsible for satisfying the following story done definitions:
- dd-4: Running aws-status.sh after successful teardown reports all five resources as absent without throwing a non-zero exit code.

## Depends on
- Task 98f7-0176-af9d-43de (aws-status.sh must exist)
- Task 35fe-b58b-2217-428f (aws-teardown.sh must exist)

## File to create
`tests/scripts/test-aws-teardown-then-status.sh`

## Implementation

Use sandbox-cd pattern with a stateful aws mock backed by STATE_FILE:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
source "$REPO_ROOT/tests/lib/assert.sh"

SANDBOX=$(mktemp -d /tmp/aws-composition-test.XXXXXX)
STATE_FILE=$(mktemp /tmp/mock-state.XXXXXX)
trap "rm -rf '$SANDBOX'; rm -f '$STATE_FILE'" EXIT

# Create dso stub
mkdir -p "$SANDBOX/.claude/scripts"
cat > "$SANDBOX/.claude/scripts/dso" << 'STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
case "$2" in
  review_telemetry.bucket_name) echo "test-bucket" ;;
  review_telemetry.lambda_function_name) echo "test-fn" ;;
  review_telemetry.iam_role_name) echo "test-role" ;;
  review_telemetry.log_group_name) echo "test-log" ;;
esac
STUB
chmod +x "$SANDBOX/.claude/scripts/dso"

# Stateful aws mock:
# - On delete calls: append resource name to STATE_FILE
# - On status/get calls: check STATE_FILE with grep for resource name → return absent if found
cat > "$SANDBOX/aws" << AWSMOCK
#!/usr/bin/env bash
case "$*" in
  *"delete-function"*) echo "test-fn" >> "$STATE_FILE"; exit 0 ;;
  *"delete-role "*) echo "test-role" >> "$STATE_FILE"; exit 0 ;;
  *"delete-bucket"*) echo "test-bucket" >> "$STATE_FILE"; exit 0 ;;
  *"delete-log-group"*) echo "test-log" >> "$STATE_FILE"; exit 0 ;;
  *"delete-role-policy"*|*"detach-role-policy"*|*"list-role-policies"*|*"list-attached-role-policies"*|*"s3 rm"*) exit 0 ;;
  *"get-function"*) grep -q 'test-fn' "$STATE_FILE" && exit 1; echo '{}' ;;
  *"get-bucket-lifecycle"*|*"get-public-access-block"*|*"get-bucket-encryption"*) grep -q 'test-bucket' "$STATE_FILE" && exit 1; echo '{}' ;;
  *"get-role"*) grep -q 'test-role' "$STATE_FILE" && exit 1; echo '{}' ;;
  *"describe-log-groups"*) grep -q 'test-log' "$STATE_FILE" && exit 1; echo '{"logGroups":[]}' ;;
  *"filter-log-events"*) echo '{"events":[]}' ;;
  *) echo '{}' ;;
esac
AWSMOCK
chmod +x "$SANDBOX/aws"
export PATH="$SANDBOX:$PATH"

cd "$SANDBOX"

# Run teardown
bash "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry/aws-teardown.sh" --user-approved
assert_eq "$?" 0 "teardown should exit 0"

# Run status — should report all-absent, still exit 0
STATUS_OUT=$(bash "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry/aws-status.sh")
assert_eq "$?" 0 "aws-status.sh should exit 0 after teardown"

# Assert all resources absent
echo "$STATUS_OUT" | jq -e '.schema_version == 1' || assert_fail "schema_version must be 1"
echo "$STATUS_OUT" | jq -e '.bucket.present == false' || assert_fail ".bucket.present must be false"
echo "$STATUS_OUT" | jq -e '.lambda.present == false' || assert_fail ".lambda.present must be false"
echo "$STATUS_OUT" | jq -e '.iam_role.present == false' || assert_fail ".iam_role.present must be false"
echo "$STATUS_OUT" | jq -e '.log_group.present == false' || assert_fail ".log_group.present must be false"
echo "$STATUS_OUT" | jq -e '.metrics.last_24h_event_count == 0' || assert_fail ".metrics.last_24h_event_count must be 0"

print_summary
```

CRITICAL: STATE_FILE is created by mktemp (not touch) and cleaned by trap. The mock checks for resource name via grep on STATE_FILE (not file existence) — grep -q 'test-fn' determines if lambda was deleted.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Unit tests pass (exit 0)
  Verify: TEST_CMD=$(.claude/scripts/dso read-config commands.test_unit) && [ -n "$TEST_CMD" ] && $TEST_CMD
- [ ] Lint passes (exit 0)
  Verify: LINT_CMD=$(.claude/scripts/dso read-config commands.lint) && [ -n "$LINT_CMD" ] && $LINT_CMD
- [ ] Format check passes (exit 0)
  Verify: FORMAT_CHECK_CMD=$(.claude/scripts/dso read-config commands.format_check) && [ -n "$FORMAT_CHECK_CMD" ] && $FORMAT_CHECK_CMD
- [ ] Integration test file exists and is executable
  Verify: test -x tests/scripts/test-aws-teardown-then-status.sh
- [ ] shellcheck passes
  Verify: shellcheck tests/scripts/test-aws-teardown-then-status.sh
- [ ] Integration test passes
  Verify: bash tests/scripts/test-aws-teardown-then-status.sh
- [ ] Test asserts all 5 resources absent and schema_version==1
  Verify: grep -E 'present.*false' tests/scripts/test-aws-teardown-then-status.sh && grep 'schema_version' tests/scripts/test-aws-teardown-then-status.sh && grep 'last_24h_event_count.*0' tests/scripts/test-aws-teardown-then-status.sh

## Retry Budget
MAX_ATTEMPTS: 3 (sonnet model)
On 3 consecutive sonnet failures: escalate to opus with full diagnostic context (all 3 failure messages)
On 3 consecutive opus failures (6 total): escalate to user with full failure history
If MAX_AGENTS: 0 at sonnet→opus escalation time: skip opus step, escalate to user immediately

AC amendment (gap analysis): Integration test should also verify schema_version and all per-resource attribute fields are present (not just .present==false) when resources ARE present before teardown. Add a pre-teardown status check:
1. Run aws-status.sh BEFORE teardown (all resources present in mock)
2. Assert .bucket.lifecycle_tier, .lambda.function_url, .iam_role.trust_policy_includes_lambda, .log_group.retention_days are all present in the output
3. THEN run teardown + post-teardown status check (existing dd-4 verification)
This guards against the schema doc diverging from the script's actual output.
